newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Protesters clash with police in central Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Protesters clash with police in central Bogota.

text.p: Protesters armed with rocks, sticks and bottles clashed with riot police in Bogota's main plaza on Tuesday, where up to 30,000 people gathered outside Congress to support a nationwide strike by public sector workers.
Witnesses said the clash, between a group of about 200 student-aged protesters and 50 police, erupted after a youth was arrested and roughed up by police after tossing a firecracker at them.

There were no immediate reports of injuries, but tensions flared as demonstrators, some using handkerchiefs and sweaters to cover their faces, picked up chunks of pavement from historic Plaza Bolivar square to hurl at police crouching behind plastic shields.
Some protesters, apparently expecting police to charge the square, set up makeshift barricades but security forces remained on the perimeter, a Reuter photographer and television camerman said.
Armored personnel carriers were positioned on side streets and police helicopters hovered overhead.

The demonstrators who clashed with police were a small minority of the 25,000 to 30,000 people who poured into the square late on Tuesday to back a nationwide public workers' strike that began at midnight Monday (0500 GMT Tuesday). Most of the peaceful protesters left the square shortly after the violence erupted.
